tip: A comparative followed by a bare genitive means than, with no separate word for it: холоднее осени (khaladneye oseni = colder than autumn).
бы plus a past-tense verb means would; бы never changes, the verb carries gender and number: бы выучили (by vyuchili = would learn).
следовало бы plus an infinitive means should or ought to: следовало бы подождать (sledavala by padazhdat = ought to wait).
кто (kto) becomes кого when it is the object (whom): кого бы ты пригласил (kavo by ty priglasil = whom would you invite).
In conditionals the past verb still shows gender: была бы (byla by = would be, feminine); a man would say был бы (byl by).
A short passive participle works like is done and agrees with its subject in gender: уже сделана (uzhe sdelana = is already done), feminine.
из plus the genitive means out of and mirrors в (v) plus accusative for going in: из дома (iz doma = out of the house).
Use где for where pointing at a place, marking location rather than motion: ресторан, где (restaran, gde = the restaurant where).
пользоваться (polzavatsya) takes the instrumental, so which appears as которым: телефон, которым я пользуюсь (telefon, katorym ya polzuyus = the phone I use).
The person receiving something goes in the dative: передай мне (pereday mne = pass me). мне is the dative of я (ya).
который (katoryy) agrees with its noun in gender and number, but its case comes from its own clause: в которой (v katoroy = in which), feminine, prepositional after в.
на моём месте is the set phrase for in my place: на моём месте (na mayom meste = if I were you). месте is prepositional after на.
Unreal conditionals put бы in both halves: если бы ты спросил, я бы ответил (yesli by ty sprasil, ya by atvetil = if you had asked, I would have answered).
As ... as is такой же plus an adjective plus как: такой же большой, как (takoy zhe balshoy, kak = as big as).
свой (svoy) means one's own and points back to the subject, replacing мой (moy) or его (yevo) when they equal the doer: своё имя (svayo imya = your own name).
ближе pairs with к plus the dative to say closer to: ближе к школе (blizhe k shkole = closer to school).
было бы plus an adjective plus an infinitive makes an impersonal it would be: было бы полезно (byla by palezna = it would be useful).
Superlatives use самый (samyy) before the adjective, both agreeing with the noun: самая холодная зима (samaya khalodnaya zima = the coldest winter), feminine.
на plus an amount tells you by how much with a comparative: старше на два года (starshe na dva goda = older by two years).
кто counts as singular, so its verb stays singular even after plural те: те, кто опоздал (te, kto apazdal = those who were late).
Russian doubles the negative, ни plus a second negator не: ни с чем не сравнить (ni s chem ne sravnit = cannot be compared to anything).
Negative commands normally use the imperfective verb: не трогай (ne trogay = don't touch), not the perfective тронь (tron).
всё before a comparative means more and more: всё выше и выше (vsyo vyshe i vyshe = higher and higher).
та (ta) becomes той in the genitive of comparison: не легче той (ne legche toy = no easier than that one), feminine matching задача (zadacha).
запомни (zapomni = remember) is the informal command to one person. For formal or plural, add -те: запомните (zapomnite).
сюда (syuda = to here) marks motion toward the speaker. A static location would use здесь (zdes = here) instead.
давайте (davayte = let's) plus a perfective we-form makes a suggestion: давайте закончим (davayte zakonchim = let's finish).
мне (mne = to me) is the dative of я, marking who gets shown something: покажите мне (pakazhite mne = show me).
лучшая (luchshaya = best) is the irregular superlative of хороший (kharoshiy = good), not a самый form.
становится (stanovitsya = becomes) plus a comparative like теплее (teplee = warmer) expresses a gradual change.
